items.summary: Vercel Labs' open-source (Apache-2.0) computer-use tool: an agent reads a desktop app's accessibility tree as structured JSON and clicks, types and manages windows by element reference, with no screenshot pixel-guessing. It ships as a CLI and an MCP server for macOS (incl. Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux, and passed 20,000 GitHub stars within days of its November 6 public release.
items.title: agent-desktop: Vercel's open-source CLI that lets agents operate desktop apps without screenshots (public Nov 6, 20k stars in days)

items.summary: An open-source (MIT), self-hosted automation hub for command-line agents such as Claude Code and Codex: cron jobs, GitHub issues and webhooks start an agent round that exits when done, and only decisions like deleting data, restarting a service or spending money surface as an approval card via Feishu, Slack, Discord or desktop notification — while it waits, no process runs and no tokens are spent. Zero runtime dependencies; 4,200+ GitHub stars in its first week since the November 3 release.
items.title: Agent Autoloop: Open-source background hub that runs CLI agents from cron, issues and webhooks, asking you only when a decision is needed (released Nov 3, 4,200+ stars)

items.summary: An open-source (AGPL-3.0) platform for AI coworkers: each one has a job, memory, skills and its own computer, and works on a schedule or webhook trigger, powered by a ChatGPT or Claude subscription you already pay for, your own API keys, or a local model. Coworkers ask before they send, pay or delete anything, and the whole stack is self-hostable; it launched on Product Hunt on November 5, taking #3 Product of the Day.
items.title: Rerun: Open-source, self-hostable team of AI coworkers, each with memory, skills and its own computer, working on schedules and triggers (Product Hunt, Nov 5)
